The function  $y=f(x)$ is defined on $x\in (-\infty ,-2]\cup (0,\infty ).$ Find ${lim}_{x\to \,-2}f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
From the graph, we see that it is not possible to approach $x=-2$ from the right. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{2}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

When we approach $x=-2$ from the left, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{2}^{-}}f(x)=-1.
$$

Since ${lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}f(x),$ we  conclude  that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-2}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{3}^{-}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

On the other hand, when we approach $x=-3$ from the right, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{3}^{+}}f(x)=2.
$$

Since ${lim}_{x\to \,-{3}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to \,-{3}^{+}}f(x),$ we  conclude  that
 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-3}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273766/assets/884ec8c4d7e079915b7b6a21a2008514bc201580b447dcfc0f9c4007e60d00dc.png)

Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above? 

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,-2}f(x)=-2$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=-1$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{2}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,-{2}^{+}}f(x)=-2.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,-2}f(x)=-2.$

- Statement II is true. Both limits ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)$ do not exist because the function $f(x)$ is not given in the interval $[0,2).$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

- Statement III is false. As $x$ approaches $2$ from the left and right we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)=\text{DNE},\,{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x)=-1.
$$

Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x).$

In conclusion, only statements I and II are true.
